text: 🇲🇽🎨 Public art schools: 1.85 billion pesos, an investment without precedent in 40 years, and no more enrollment fees. — Claudia Curiel de Icaza, Secretary of Culture In two years, 2,352 spaces were renovated in the schools of INBAL, INAH, the Film Training Center and the Carlos Chávez Orchestra School, which now has its own building after 37 years. Enrollment fees were eliminated "to guarantee free artistic education." Support for artists rose 45%, from 1,840 to 2,658 million pesos, reaching more than 180,000 artists. Cultural programming grew 32%: 520,000 activities in all 32 states, with 50 million attendees.

text: 🇲🇽📱 "The platforms have to prove to us that they are safe places for minors." — Mario Delgado, Secretary of Public Education "With all the artificial intelligence they have, of course they are capable of detecting in time and removing content that incites violence." Delgado noted that similar steps are being taken in other countries, including the United States. Sheinbaum said Meta's settlement in the big US trial includes getting rid of likes, limiting minors to a couple of hours a day and shutting the platform off at night: "That shows that greater responsibility is possible." Schools are also reinforcing the "ABC of Emotions" program, with parent assemblies, confidential mailboxes and the Línea de la Vida helpline for psychological support.

🇲🇽📈 <u>Analysts Raise Mexico's 2026 Growth Forecast</u>

Banxico's October survey of 42 domestic and foreign analysis firms raised Mexico's 2026 GDP forecast from 1.3% to 1.4%, while expected year-end core inflation fell from 4.0% to 3.89% (El Economista). Headline inflation is seen closing 2026 at 3.87%, with the policy rate holding at 6.50% and the peso at 17.50 per dollar.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The Army's Own Files Admit Dirty War "Illegality"</u>

Military Justice Prosecutor documents obtained by Fábrica de Periodismo and Artículo 19 show the Mexican Army itself recognized the "illegality" of its Dirty War operations: clandestine detentions and interrogations at Campo Militar 1 and the Pie de la Cuesta air base, and extrajudicial executions. The files reconstruct the "death flights" over Guerrero from 1974 to 1979, where victims were shot in the back of the head and dumped into the Pacific from Arava planes. Defense Secretary Hermenegildo Cuenca Díaz authorized the operation, including bonus pay for the crews.

🇲🇽🏪 <u>CDMX: Zero Closures for Small Shops, No More Shakedown Inspections</u>

Clara Brugada's government launched "Código Avisa," a traffic-light inspection model built to stop extortion: zero closures for low-impact businesses with fixable violations. Corner stores, stationers, cafés, laundries and mechanics get three warnings before any suspension, restaurants two, bars and clubs one. Every visit now requires a verifiable digital order, and INVEA inspectors carry QR-coded smart IDs. Selling alcohol to minors, violence or over-capacity still mean immediate closure.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>No, Mexico Isn't Jailing Memes</u>

Presidential Legal Counsel Luisa María Alcalde took apart the "Ley Antimemes" panic: the new Article 403 Bis punishes using official logos, domains or documents to impersonate government institutions in order to commit a crime, with 1 to 5 years in prison and fines of 1,000 to 10,000 UMA. The targets: fake IMSS sites offering pension "recalculations" for a deposit, fake UIF and Hacienda pages, and AI deepfakes of Sheinbaum selling bogus Pemex investments.

"There has to be the intent to deceive, the intent to commit a crime, and to pass yourself off as the government."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>After Torreón, Sheinbaum Moves to Make Big Tech Pull Violent Content</u>

Following the attack at Secundaria 13 in Torreón, Sheinbaum set up a working group under the Presidency's Legal Counsel, with the Digital Transformation Agency, SSPC, SEP, the National Intelligence Center and experts from UNAM and IPN, to draft a decree. It will oblige platforms like TikTok, Meta and Instagram to detect, remove and report content that directly incites violence, coordinate with Mexican authorities, and push age verification on social networks.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>"Captain Sol" Falls: Huachicol Fiscal Operator Arrested</u>

Mexico's FGR arrested Miguel Ángel Solano Ruiz, "El Capitán Sol," a former Navy corvette captain and ex-PGR intelligence officer identified as one of the main operators of the huachicol fiscal ring that moved smuggled fuel through customs with Navy commanders and the Farías Laguna brothers. He was detained in Zapopan, handed to the organized-crime prosecutors and sent to the Altiplano maximum-security prison.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Pemex refining up 22%: diesel +49%, gasoline +23%</u>

According to El Financiero, Pemex's national refining system produced 22% more fuel in August 2026 than a year earlier: gasoline output rose 23% and diesel 49%. Refineries processed 1.208 million barrels a day (+15%), and the Olmeca refinery at Dos Bocas ran 252,471 b/d, up 94% year on year.

That is why crude exports fell to 276,000 b/d: the oil is being refined at home instead of shipped out raw. Domestic sales rose 15% for gasoline and 17% for diesel, and Pemex says the extra fuel is cutting imports, just as Washington threatens to restrict US diesel exports.

🇲🇽💻 <u>Public-university grads build 279 government apps and save 14 billion pesos</u>

The Agency for Digital Transformation (ATDT) says its in-house Software Factory, made up of 300 young graduates of public universities, has built 279 digital products. Building them in-house instead of hiring private contractors has saved the government more than 14 billion pesos.

Its new AI Factory is now developing tools for customs, invoice-fraud detection, patent assignment at IMPI and 24/7 citizen service. Under José Antonio Peña Merino, the state is building its own technology instead of renting it from consultancies.
